belongs_to: Try This: 'What is the length of the shortest path between the ant and the laddu?' (cuboid 30 cm long with square 12 x 12 end faces; continues the ant-and-laddu problem of the previous page)
description: Three drawings in a row, all light green with fine vertical stripes (the stripes are only texture). CENTRE: a cuboid drawn in 3D, long side horizontal, with a double-headed arrow above its top edge labelled '30 cm'. Three hidden edges at the back-left bottom corner are dashed (one vertical, two horizontal). A yellow laddu (ball) is stuck on the back (left) end face near its lower left corner, with a curved arrow from the text 'laddu (stuck to the back of the box)' pointing at it; a black ant sits on the front (right) end face near its upper edge. A curved black arrow leaves the left end towards the left drawing and another leaves the right end towards the right drawing. LEFT DRAWING (the back end face laid flat as a 12 x 12 square): double-headed arrow '12 cm' under the bottom edge, double-headed arrow '12 cm' along the left edge. A dashed vertical line runs from the top edge straight down to the laddu; a double-headed arrow '6 cm' above the top edge spans from that dashed line to the RIGHT edge. The laddu has a red dot at its centre (the point). A dashed horizontal line runs from the laddu to the right edge; a vertical double-headed arrow '1 cm' on the right side spans from that dashed line down to the bottom edge. So the laddu is 6 cm from the right edge and 1 cm above the bottom edge. RIGHT DRAWING (the front end face laid flat as a 12 x 12 square): '12 cm' double-headed arrow above the top edge, '12 cm' double-headed arrow along the right edge. The ant (red dot on its body) is joined by a dashed horizontal line to the left edge, with a vertical double-headed arrow '1 cm' at the top-left spanning from the top edge to that dashed line; a dashed vertical line runs from the ant down to the bottom edge, with a double-headed arrow '6 cm' under the bottom edge spanning from the left edge to that dashed line. So the ant is 1 cm below the top edge and 6 cm from the left edge. Data in the figure: cuboid 30 cm long, ends 12 cm x 12 cm; laddu on one end face (6 cm from one side, 1 cm from the bottom), ant on the opposite end face (6 cm from one side, 1 cm from the top).
unclear: The left face is drawn as seen from behind, so the '6 cm' on the left drawing is measured to its right edge while the '6 cm' on the right drawing is measured from its left edge; both are 6 cm from the same long side only if the mirroring is as intended (not stated).
The cuboid is not drawn to scale (30 cm drawn only about 2.5 times the 12 cm end).

belongs_to: 'Here are some of the ways of unfolding the cuboid.' Two nets of the 30 x 12 x 12 cuboid with the ant-laddu line drawn; the text then works out the second case with d^2 = 24^2 + 32^2, d = sqrt(1600) = 40 cm (first case gives 42 cm)
description: Two nets side by side (green faces, alternate faces have fine horizontal/vertical stripe texture which carries no meaning). Each net = a column of 4 equal long rectangles stacked vertically (the four long faces, each about 2 times as wide as tall) plus two small squares (the two 12 x 12 end faces). LEFT NET (T-shape, 6 faces): the four long rectangles are stacked in one column (4 rectangles, no gaps); the top rectangle has one small square attached to its left side and one small square attached to its right side. A yellow laddu sits in the left square (near its left/centre, at the height of the middle of the square) and a small black ant sits in the right square (near its left part, same height). One horizontal blue line joins laddu and ant through the top rectangle; the label '42 cm' is written just under it on the top rectangle. RIGHT NET (6 faces): again a column of 4 long rectangles stacked vertically (rows 1 to 4 from the top). One small square is attached on the RIGHT side of row 1 (top row) and one small square on the LEFT side of row 3. The laddu (yellow ball) is in the left square (row 3 level), the ant in the right square (row 1 level, near its left part). Blue lines: a long straight line (the shortest path, the hypotenuse) from the laddu up and to the right across rows 3, 2, 1 to the ant; a horizontal blue segment from the laddu to the right, at laddu height, ending just OUTSIDE the right edge of the column (below the right square), labelled '32 cm' under it (it passes through row 3); and a vertical blue segment going up from that end to the ant's level, in the white space under the right square, labelled '24 cm' (written rotated, right of the vertical line). The horizontal and vertical segments meet at a right angle, so laddu - corner - ant is a right triangle with legs 32 cm and 24 cm. Printed numbers: 42 cm (left net), 32 cm and 24 cm (right net).
unclear: Exact placement of the laddu and ant inside their squares is only approximate (laddu near the centre of its square, ant near the left-centre of its square).
The nets are not drawn to scale (long face about 2 times, not 2.5 times, the end square).

Whether the two squares are attached at the TOP row of each column (left net) and at rows 1 and 3 (right net) is read from the picture; the figure is a drawing of a net, so the face textures were not treated as meaningful.

belongs_to: 'Let us visualise the projection of a line.' Fig. 4.2 (two drawings: line parallel to the plane, and a tilted line)
description: Two drawings side by side under one caption 'Fig. 4.2'. In each, a tall slanted plane (parallelogram with vertical left/right sides) stands upright; on the plane a thin straight segment (the projection) slopes up to the right; in front of the plane (to its right) a thick straight segment (the actual line) is drawn; two dashed lines (projectors) join the two ends of the projection to the two ends of the thick segment; at each end of the projection a small right-angle square marks that the projector meets the plane at 90 degrees (2 right-angle marks per drawing, 4 in all). A curved grey arrow with the word 'Projection' points to the thin segment on the plane (left drawing: label on the left of the plane; right drawing: label on the right). LEFT DRAWING: the thick segment is parallel to the plane and has the same direction and the same length as its projection (so the dashed projectors form a parallelogram with both segments). RIGHT DRAWING: the thick segment is tilted relative to the plane (it slopes up to the right much less steeply than the projection, and is drawn longer), so its projection on the plane is a different, shorter segment; the dashed projectors still run perpendicular to the plane. No numbers.
unclear: Whether the right drawing's actual line is longer than its projection (it looks about 1.7 times longer) is visual only; no lengths are printed.
